title: Delhi Sultanate
summary: From 1206 until Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi in 1526, a succession of Muslim dynasties, among them the Khaljis, Tughlaqs, Sayyids and Lodis, ruled northern India from Delhi. Under the Khaljis its reach extended into southern India. The sultanate saw inland and sea trade grow and towns multiply, Persian translation of scriptures, and a blending of Hindu and Muslim building styles into Indo-Islamic architecture, seen at the Qutb Minar complex.

uncertainty.note: Dated from Qutb al-Din Aibak assuming independent authority in 1206 to the defeat of Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat in 1526.

as_recorded.value: in 1206, and the Delhi Sultanate continued until 1526
Built in the early 13th century a few kilometres south of Delhi

where.modern_name: Delhi, India (stand-in pin for the imperial capital of the Delhi Sultanate)

importance.justification: Three centuries of Muslim rule over northern India that shaped its architecture and culture (R3 D3 T3 L3).

related.because: Razia Sultana ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1236 to 1240 as its first and only female sovereign.
The Qutb Minar complex in Delhi was initiated by early sultans of the Mamluk dynasty.
Babur's victory over Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat in 1526 terminated the Delhi Sultanate and founded the Mughal Empire.
